excerpts.text: Born in 1897 in Philadelphia, Marian Anderson showed an incredible singing voice at a very young age. She sang in her church choir and later traveled across Europe to perform in front of large crowds. In 1939, she sang on the steps of the Lincoln Memorial in Washington, D.C., drawing a huge audience of seventy-five thousand listeners.

In the winter of 1912, young Leo rode in a crowded steamship across the cold Atlantic Ocean with his mother and sister. They carried two heavy wooden trunks filled with clothes and family photographs. When the ship finally docked at Ellis Island, Leo gripped his mother's hand tightly as they stood in line to answer questions from the inspectors.

Honeybees have six legs and two pairs of wings that beat two hundred times every second. Worker bees fly from flower to flower gathering sticky pollen on their hairy legs. When they return to the hive, they perform a special movement called a waggle dance to show other bees where to find the sweetest nectar.
